The origin of the Haiku can be traced back to the 17th century, when it was first introduced to Japan from China. The Chinese poet Li Bai, known for his profound and poetic works, introduced the concept of the Haiku to Japan. He wrote the poem "The Return of the Moon" in 1058 AD, which became the first known Haiku in Japan.

The Haiku has since become an integral part of Japanese culture and literature, serving as a powerful tool for expressing emotions, capturing moments, and conveying spiritual insights. It continues to be celebrated and appreciated worldwide, particularly in Japan, where it is deeply ingrained in the national identity and cultural heritage.
